vo.text: Did Mom take her pills? Nobody knows. The group chat doesn't.
About half of patients don't take their medicines as prescribed. An assistant is already in the room. It just can't remember.
Tend is a real MCP server. The Alexa+ display on top is simulated, and says so everywhere.
Ask, and the display calls the server through a real MCP client.
Skip an hour. After sixty minutes of grace, the server sends one escalation.
One alert, once per slot, enforced by a database key. The message is a template, so it can't give advice.
Two separate processes hammer the check sixty times. Still exactly one alert.
A late dose resolves the alert with a follow-up. No second message.
The caregiver sees the same thing on a phone. The week, the alerts, and a timeline of what happened.
Try a name with an advice word, and Tend refuses to store it. It never gives medical advice.
A normal schedule is proposed first. Nothing saves until you confirm.
A standard MCP client, the Inspector, connects, lists all eight tools, and calls each one.
Sixty-one tests. Thirteen browser tests. Green builds on Windows and Linux. Zero dollars. No AI model.
Tend. A real MCP server that remembers. Open source, built for the Amazon Developer Hackathon.
